resourceProfile.assessment: The complete English and Greek source scope, review metadata, glossary, and project concept references were available locally.

automatedQuality.summary: Translation review metadata, queue validation, typecheck, 79 test files with 462 tests, complete build, 39 IIS rules with 61 route cases, and 724 generated-link checks passed.

linguisticCritique.summary: A bounded Greek pass identified 25 actionable formula, terminology, grammar, and technical-clarity defects across electrical, trigonometric, thermal, unit, and wire-gauge content; all 25 were corrected.

competentHumanReview.summary: No competent Greek human review was performed in this cycle; changed IDs remain machine-drafted.

publicationAuthorization.summary: No merge, publication, deployment, or residual-risk authorization was requested or granted.

findings.summary: The Joule example described a power rate as joules per second without stating the equivalent power.
evidence: The previous conclusion used a literal joules-per-second phrasing.
findings.resolution: Clarified the result as 7,2 W or 72 J in 10 seconds.

findings.summary: The heat-transfer bullet used a generic Greek word for material where equipment was intended.
evidence: The previous bullet referred generically to material alongside air and liquid.
findings.resolution: Changed the final term to εξοπλισμό.

findings.summary: The sine formula retained the English side name opposite.
evidence: The previous formula contained the English word opposite.
findings.resolution: Localized the side name as απέναντι πλευρά.

findings.summary: The cosine formula retained the English side names adjacent and hypotenuse.
evidence: The previous formula contained adjacent and hypotenuse in English.
findings.resolution: Localized the terms as διπλανή πλευρά and υποτείνουσα.

findings.summary: The tangent formula retained English names for both triangle sides.
evidence: The previous formula contained opposite and adjacent in English.
findings.resolution: Localized the terms as απέναντι πλευρά and διπλανή πλευρά.

findings.summary: The inverse-sine formula retained English triangle-side terminology.
evidence: The previous inverse formula used opposite and hypotenuse.
findings.resolution: Localized the terms as απέναντι πλευρά and υποτείνουσα.

findings.summary: The inverse-cosine formula retained English triangle-side terminology.
evidence: The previous inverse formula used adjacent and hypotenuse.
findings.resolution: Localized the terms as διπλανή πλευρά and υποτείνουσα.

findings.summary: The inverse-tangent formula retained English triangle-side terminology.
evidence: The previous inverse formula used opposite and adjacent.
findings.resolution: Localized the terms as απέναντι πλευρά and διπλανή πλευρά.

findings.summary: The temperature-difference equivalence was phrased imprecisely.
evidence: The previous bullet did not clearly state the one-kelvin and one-degree-Celsius difference equivalence.
findings.resolution: Rephrased the statement as a 1 K temperature difference equaling a 1 °C difference.

findings.summary: The electrical-heating conclusion used a rounded or unclear time expression.
evidence: The previous conclusion did not preserve the validated 523 s result clearly.
findings.resolution: Restored the approximate ideal time and the 80-percent-efficiency result of 523 s.

findings.summary: The phase-change explanation used an imprecise phrase for the material's phase.
evidence: The previous paragraph used a generic or awkward phase description.
findings.resolution: Changed it to the precise phrase φάση του υλικού.

findings.summary: The limitation paragraph referred to specific heat instead of specific heat capacity.
evidence: The previous Greek terminology did not distinguish specific heat capacity precisely.
findings.resolution: Changed the term to ειδική θερμοχωρητικότητα and retained the practical limitations.

findings.summary: The heat-flux description used a less precise translation for heat-flux density.
evidence: The previous description did not consistently use the technical Greek term for heat-flux density.
findings.resolution: Aligned the description with πυκνότητα θερμικής ροής.

findings.summary: The heat-flux summary was indirect and less clear than the source concept.
evidence: The previous summary did not state the rate of heat transfer per unit area directly.
findings.resolution: Changed it to Ο ρυθμός μεταφοράς θερμότητας ανά μονάδα επιφάνειας.

findings.summary: The heat-flux definition did not use the preferred technical Greek term.
evidence: The previous definition described q'' with a generic heat-flow term.
findings.resolution: Defined q'' as πυκνότητα θερμικής ροής in W/m².

findings.summary: The definition paragraph blurred heat capacity and heat-flux density terminology.
evidence: The previous paragraph used inconsistent terms when contrasting stored energy with transfer rate.
findings.resolution: Rewrote the contrast using πυκνότητα θερμικής ροής consistently.

findings.summary: The worked-example section title was translated with an overly generic label.
evidence: The previous title did not clearly identify the section as a calculation example.
findings.resolution: Changed it to Παράδειγμα υπολογισμού.

findings.summary: The heat-flux example title omitted the technical density concept.
evidence: The previous title used a generic heater heat-flow phrase.
findings.resolution: Changed it to Μέση πυκνότητα θερμικής ροής από θερμαντήρα.

findings.summary: The heat-flux example conclusion used an inconsistent quantity name.
evidence: The previous conclusion did not align its terminology with the heat-flux density definition.
findings.resolution: Aligned the conclusion with πυκνότητα θερμικής ροής and preserved both unit forms.

findings.summary: The conduction note used an inconsistent translation for heat flow.
evidence: The previous bullet used a generic flow term for the direction indicated by the minus sign.
findings.resolution: Changed it to θερμική ροή.

findings.summary: The convection-and-radiation paragraph used inconsistent technical capitalization and phrasing.
evidence: The previous paragraph used a lowercase or nonstandard rendering of Kelvin and less precise technical wording.
findings.resolution: Clarified the coefficients, absolute temperatures, and the unit name Kelvin.

findings.summary: The SI base-units table used an inconsistent Greek form for second.
evidence: The previous table row did not use the standard Greek unit name.
findings.resolution: Changed the unit name to δευτερόλεπτο.

findings.summary: The series-connection definition did not clearly state that current has one path.
evidence: The previous bullet used an awkward literal description of a series connection.
findings.resolution: Rewrote it as a series connection providing only one path through the components.

findings.summary: The wire-gauge comparison used an awkward phrase for stranded construction.
evidence: The previous paragraph used a literal or unnatural Greek expression for strand construction.
findings.resolution: Changed it to κατασκευή με κλώνους and clarified its effect on measured diameter.

findings.summary: The practical wire specification bullet did not clearly describe stranded conductors and their construction.
evidence: The previous bullet used vague wording for multi-strand conductors.
findings.resolution: Rewrote it with πολύκλωνους αγωγούς and κατασκευή των κλώνων.
